verdict.rationale: SigNoz is free, open-source and self-hostable via Docker, Kubernetes or Linux, so a developer can run their own instance. Community reports describe real friction for a local setup: a heavy multi-container docker-compose, Windows installs failing on sh/bash dependencies, and early docs leading with Kubernetes. missing for 10: explicit first-party docs for a lightweight local/dev quickstart, documented Windows support, and hands-on confirmation of testing instrumentation and dashboards against a local instance.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up a local or dev instance of the platform to test instrumentation and dashboards

citations.quote: Free open-source SigNoz that runs in your own infrastructure. Deploy with Docker, Kubernetes, or Linux and keep full control of your data plane.
the self-hosting setup has more containers than their whole application
It failed on dependencies on sh/bash, and they asked for Windows-specific instructions.
